short: A long boom, a budget surplus, and the second impeachment of a president.
full:
Clinton was the first Democrat elected to two terms since Roosevelt. His health care plan collapsed in 1994 and the Republicans took both houses of Congress for the first time in forty years, but he recovered by dealing with them, signing the North American Free Trade Agreement, welfare reform in 1996, and a budget agreement that produced federal surpluses from 1998.

Foreign policy was hesitant early, with no intervention during the Rwandan genocide of 1994 and slow engagement in Bosnia, and firmer later, with NATO's air campaign over Kosovo in 1999 and American brokerage of the Good Friday Agreement. The House impeached him in December 1998 for perjury and obstruction of justice arising from an affair with a White House intern; the Senate acquitted him in February 1999, and he left office with approval ratings above 60 per cent.
